ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The uniform electric field has a strength of $E = 100 \, \mathrm{V/m}$. Points A and B are $10 \, \mathrm{cm}$ apart, and the line connecting A and B forms an angle of $60^{\circ}$ with the electric field lines.

1. Find the value of $U_{BA}$.

Find the value of $U_{BA}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The uniform electric field has a strength of $E = 100\,\mathrm{V/m}$. Points A and B are $10\,\mathrm{cm}$ apart, and the line connecting A and B forms an angle of $60^{\circ}$ with the electric field lines. Find the value of $U_{BA}$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are multiple parallel arrows vertically upward, indicating that the direction of the uniform electric field is upward; point A is located at a lower position, point B is located to the upper right of A, and line segment AB goes obliquely upward from A to B, so the displacement from A to B has a component along the direction of the electric field; the angle between AB and the direction of the vertical electric field lines is marked in the figure as 60°. Reasoning: The potential difference is taken as U_BA = V_B - V_A according to the requirement in the problem. The electric potential decreases along the direction of the electric field, so when there is a displacement along the direction of the electric field from A to B, V_B is less than V_A. Use the formula U_BA = -E·AB·cosθ. Given E = 100 V/m, AB = 10 cm = 0.10 m, θ = 60°, so U_BA = -100 × 0.10 × cos60° = -100 × 0.10 × 0.5 = -5 V.
